title: EvalDocResult
description: Output of `model eval` — the runtime verdict over a document INSTANCE: which rules fired on the data, via the native-safe interpreter (the sole runtime eval engine on every target). By default this is full validation. `--relevant <json>` selects partial validation: a JSON array of current-page field/group instance paths; an omitted index or `[*]` means every repetition (ALL_SEMANTIC), while `[n]` selects one 1-based row. Global fields are auto-relevant. The INPUT --instance is a nested tree under "fields" (repeatable group = array of row objects, non-repeatable group = nested object, field = its text value; null/"" = present-but-unfilled, an absent key = no instance).

validationMode.description: present only when `--relevant` selected partial validation; absent means full validation

fired.description: the distinct error codes that fired, in first-seen order

messages.description: every message the evaluation raised, in evaluation order. Evaluated by the dm interpreter — the envelope's `engine` names who produced these

rule.description: present only when narrowed to one rule (--rule or a candidate --condition/--field)

fired.description: whether that rule fired on the document

unsupported.description: present only when the engine could NOT evaluate some construct — a CustomCondition with no registered impl, or a custom-typed value with no --predefined-types entry. Reported here, NOT silently absent from `fired` (which would read as a clean pass) — G29. `--strict-custom` turns a non-empty `unsupported` into a refusal (exit 2).

name.description: the rule's slash-path (a CustomCondition rule) or the value's instance pointer (an unregistered custom type)

code.description: the rule's error code, or a kernel formal-error code

rule.description: the firing rule's full slash-path (e.g. /Order/X); a kernel FORMAL check reports the sentinel 'formalePruefung' — a leading '/' is the author-rule discriminator

field.description: the offending field's instance pointer in canonical A12 form — no leading slash, [1] omitted, one repetition per part, e.g. Order/Items[2]/Count — the row it hit. Paste-compatible with A12 addressing

message.description: the INTERPOLATED end-user text — the authored message with $Field$/$Field.value$ tokens resolved against this document (what the user actually reads, G1)

referenced.description: the fields the rule READ (its operands), as canonical A12 instance pointers — A12's referencedFields

fillToFix.description: for an OMISSION error, the operand fields that — if filled/changed — would clear it (the kernel's refOmissionErrorResponsible); absent for a VALUE error
